## Overview

::: {.callout-warning title="Current reporting result — computationally sound, identification-qualified"}
The corrected 2026-08-09 `reporting` fit uses the exact same 50-child identity as MED-086 and passes the automatic computational gate. The interventional indirect contrast is +0.079 in off-floor probability (89% interval +0.028 to +0.148; P>0 = 0.996), while the total is +0.087 (−0.011 to +0.188; P>0 = 0.924). Numerical agreement with MED-086 is expected from the shared fitted model and current g-formula functional; it is an implementation check, not identification evidence. MED-086's session-dose calibration band extends past the shift where the indirect 89% interval first includes zero; that interval threshold is not where its median becomes zero. Power scaling also flags material prior/likelihood sensitivity. This remains a model-based decomposition under unresolved confounding and same-wave assumptions, not an identified causal route.
:::

MED-186 is the parent+100 **interventional-effects companion** to [MED-086](https://github.com/dseinternational/language-reading-predictors/tree/main/docs/models/lrp-rli-med-086). Both fit the same Phase-0 joint model, use letter-sound knowledge at t2 as the mediator, use the same signed-off adjustment set, and model nonword reading as the binary off-floor outcome $\mathbf{1}[N_{t2}>0]$. MED-086 reports the natural direct and indirect effects (NDE/NIE); MED-186 reports their randomised-interventional analogues (IDE/IIE).

_Off-floor outcome — effects are risk differences._ IDE, IIE and Total are changes in the probability of reading at least one nonword, not changes in an item count. Positive values mean that the intervention increases the probability of coming off the floor.

## Why the estimand changes

Sessions attended ($IS$) are affected by randomised group and are a common cause of the mediator and outcome through $IS\to L$ and $IS\to PA\to N$. This recanting-witness structure makes the cross-world natural effects formally unidentified. The interventional analogue instead draws the mediator from its arm-specific covariate-conditional distribution, so it remains well-defined without asking for the same child's mediator under incompatible treatment worlds.

**What the label does and does not buy** (#585 finding 2). A well-defined estimand is not an identified one. An interventional effect is identified in the presence of an exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounder only when that confounder is *measured* and integrated over — within its treated distribution in the outcome leg and its control distribution in the mediator leg. Sessions attended enter neither leg of this fit, so the functional computed here identifies the interventional target only under the same no-exposure-induced-confounding condition the natural version requires, and it reproduces the parent model's numbers exactly by construction. Treat the relabelling as a change of target, not as a robustness gain; latent general ability leaves both versions unidentified regardless.

That change does **not** make MED-186 a fully identified causal mediation analysis. Latent general ability still confounds the $L\to N$ relationship, mediator and outcome are measured in the same wave, and $IS$ is not represented in the fitted joint model. IDE/IIE are therefore weaker-assumption, model-based decompositions under the stated assumptions, not identified causal routes.

## Comparison with MED-086

The fitted probabilistic model and adjustment set are intentionally identical to MED-086. In the current fully parametric g-formula, both estimand classes draw $L$ from the same fitted covariate-conditional law; changing `estimand` changes the counterfactual interpretation and the row labels, not the numerical functional. MED-186's IIE should therefore agree with MED-086's NIE up to posterior-sampling and g-formula Monte Carlo error. Agreement is an implementation check; it is **not** evidence that shared dose causes no distortion. A material gap would first indicate non-comparable fits or Monte Carlo error, not a scientific dose-confounding result.

## Adjustment set

The set is inherited directly from MED-086: randomised group $G$, age $A$, baseline letter sounds $L_{t1}$, baseline blending $B_{t1}$, baseline word reading $WR_1$, hearing $HS$, speech production $SP$ and phonological memory $RW$, with the raw-covariate missing indicators. $WR_1$ blocks the newly recognised measured forks $LS_2\leftarrow WR_1\to NW_2$ and $LS_2\leftarrow WR_1\to PA_2\to NW_2$. As required by the floor rule, the binary outcome has no own-baseline term. Baseline expressive/receptive vocabulary is not required, and no treatment-non-descendant adjustment set can block the $L_2\leftarrow IS_1\to PA_2\to NW_2$ witness path; the correction reduces observable backdoor bias without identifying the IDE/IIE split.
